title: Lighthouse storm: two local, two cloud
prompt: Build an interactive Three.js scene of a lighthouse on a rocky island at dusk, as a single HTML file (CDN imports OK). Orbit/zoom camera, touch friendly. A button rolls in a storm: sky darkens, waves grow, rain starts, the lighthouse beam sweeps. Press again and a ship appears, gets guided in by the beam and docks. Reset clears the weather.

recording.grid: top-left DeepSeek, top-right Astra, bottom-left GLM, bottom-right Fable
recording.method: Playwright headless Chromium (ANGLE Metal), fixed-step virtual clock 30 fps. Identical timeline: storm button at 6 s, ship button at 22–24 s, reset at 40–55 s. Camera rotated to the sunlit side before recording. Local clips are 45 s and hold their last frame to fill 60 s.
recording.caveat: Ship visibility depends on the scripted camera azimuth; absence in a panel is not proof the scene has no ship.

arms.label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash EXL3
arms.finding: Water ShaderMaterial present but renders as a flat, featureless plane in calm state; the agent reviewed 13 of its own screenshots without flagging it.

arms.label: GLM-5.3 Flash EXL3
arms.finding: Gerstner vertex-shader waves with foam, keeper's hut, pier, sweeping beam cones.

arms.label: Astra (GPT-5.4, cloud)
arms.finding: Full editorial UI (chapters, prose, progress), island with buildings, whitecaps, ship guided in-frame. Loads Google Fonts.

arms.label: Fable 5 (Anthropic, cloud)
arms.finding: Minimal: small tower, flat dark sea, thin beam, two buttons.

incident: GLM rank-1 host spark-9f73 hard-wedged during the first attempt (84.6K-token prefill in flight); power-cycled, fresh containers relaunched, requalified, and the prompt was resent from a new session. Wall time above is the successful run only.
notes: Cloud arms were run by the user in their own sessions; token/timing receipts are not available for them.
DeepSeek is usually served TP4 in this lab; this run was a TP2 pack. Whether that explains the water is untested.
